# RFCs

The design documents of the extensions, one per change worth arguing about
before it is written. BatleHub's own RFCs live in that repository
(`batleforc/batlehub/docs/rfc/`); this series is the extensions', numbered
from 0001. A new one: `task rfc:new TITLE="…" SETTLES="…"` (the template is
`docs/internal/0000-rfc-template.md`); the table and the sidebar below are
generated from each document's header table by `task rfc:index`, and
`task rfc:index:check` fails the docs build when they have drifted.

<!-- BEGIN rfc-index — generated by `task rfc:index` from each RFC's header table — do not edit by hand -->

Of the eighteen below, one is accepted, fifteen are drafts and two are parked.

**In the works** — fifteen proposals still being written or reviewed.

| RFC | Status | Closes | What it settles |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [0002 — Headless engine](/rfc/0002-headless-engine-mcp) | Draft | A.13 — the same operations for the developer's agents and for CI: the editor is driven by both | The native engine: every operation of the JDT bundle (rename, generate, inspections, fix-all) as a CLI subcommand and an MCP tool — the crate, its platform matrix, per-platform VSIX, signing and fuzzing, the auth model, what never leaves the machine |
| [0003 — Orchestrated runs](/rfc/0003-server-run-step-kinds) | Draft | A.4 — acceptance runs: processes started in order, waited ready, stopped in reverse; the managed process every satellite starts through | The orchestrator and the managed process: ordered steps with readiness probes and reverse stop in `launch.json`, and the one way anything long-lived is started in the whole series — a declared memory cap, a readiness probe, a clean stop, its peak RSS recorded. The server kinds (Tomcat, Jetty, WildFly, Karaf) are [RFC 0017](/rfc/0017-server-kinds), parked |
| [0004 — Run-config sources](/rfc/0004-run-config-sources) | Draft | A.13, A.4 — the devfile, Taskfile and Makefile commands a team already has, as run configurations | Reading devfile commands (never writing), Taskfile and Makefile targets as run-configuration templates |
| [0005 — Inspection profiles](/rfc/0005-shared-inspection-profiles) | Draft | A.9, A.13 — a team inspection profile, every disabled rule with its reason | Team inspection profiles as committed files, every disabled rule carrying its rationale, precedence with user overrides |
| [0006 — Project config](/rfc/0006-shared-project-config) | Draft | A.12 — project-wide settings shared in the repository, the `.idea` equivalent | Everything under .batlehub/java/: schema, precedence with settings.json, what is committed and what is not (the overlay never is) |
| [0007 — IntelliJ import](/rfc/0007-intellij-import-full) | Draft | A.4, A.12 — the switch itself: what a developer configured in IntelliJ arrives with them | Beyond phase 4's run configurations: code style, live templates, file templates, keymap customisations, inspection profiles |
| [0008 — Kotlin](/rfc/0008-kotlin-satellite) | Draft | A.10 — Kotlin and mixed Java + Kotlin modules (Team B) | A Kotlin language server (JetBrains' official LSP vs fwcd), Gradle Kotlin DSL, mixed Java + Kotlin modules on the core's project model |
| [0009 — Scala](/rfc/0009-scala-satellite) | Draft | A.10 — Scala through Metals on the core's JDK (Team B) | Metals integration with the core's JDK, explorer and run configurations |
| [0010 — Spring Boot](/rfc/0010-spring-boot-satellite) | Draft | A.11 — Spring Boot (Team A) | Detection, properties completion, bean navigation, dashboard; relationship with vmware.vscode-spring-boot |
| [0011 — Quarkus](/rfc/0011-quarkus-satellite) | Draft | A.11 — Quarkus (Team A) | Dev mode as a managed process, properties, extensions; relationship with redhat.vscode-quarkus |
| [0012 — Chain completion](/rfc/0012-chain-completion) | Draft | A.6 — chain completion | Chained-call completion in the JDT bundle, its cost and ranking |
| [0013 — Spell checking](/rfc/0013-spell-checking) | Draft | A.6 — spell-checking in identifiers and comments | Identifiers and comments spell-check inside the inspections flow, or a bridge to an existing extension |
| [0014 — BatleHub theme](/rfc/0014-batlehub-theme) | Draft | Product — BatleHub's identity in the editor | A BatleHub colour theme extension (dark, light, high-contrast) derived from BatleHub's DESIGN.md; on the gallery for whoever wants it — the pack neither installs nor recommends it |
| [0015 — Generate shortcuts](/rfc/0015-generate-shortcuts) | Draft | A.8 — Builder pattern, live templates with surround-with: the shortcuts a team leaving IntelliJ misses first (Team A) | The code-generation shortcuts Appendix A.8 still owes — the Builder pattern, with-methods, surround-with — each a bundle delegate and so an agent tool, the list taken from Team A's diary rather than guessed |
| [0016 — Inspections growth](/rfc/0016-inspections-growth) | Draft | A.9 — inspections and quality, the moat RFC 0001 §2 names | Where inspections come from: SonarLint bridged for breadth, the bundle grown only where a team diary names a missing rule or a quick fix; type-aware rules, how they are proven, and the admission policy that keeps a wrong rule out |

**Ready to build** — one accepted and waiting to be built.

| RFC | Status | Closes | What it settles |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [0001 — Java extensions](/rfc/0001-java-env) | Accepted | — | How BatleHub closes the gap between VS Code and IntelliJ IDEA for Java: one core extension that orchestrates the Red Hat language stack and adds what it lacks, the contract a later satellite plugs into, and what is deliberately deferred to its own RFC |

**Parked** — two kept so the idea is not lost, waiting for the trigger each one names — not promises.

| RFC | Status | Closes | What it settles |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [0017 — Server kinds](/rfc/0017-server-kinds) | Parked | A.4 — application server configurations (Tomcat, Jetty, WildFly, Karaf) | Tomcat, Jetty, WildFly and Karaf as managed-process kinds over RFC 0003's orchestrator — split out of RFC 0003, parked until someone on a team deploys to one |
| [0018 — Rust syntactic tier](/rfc/0018-rust-syntactic-tier) | Parked | A.13 — usable before indexing | A small standalone Rust language server (tree-sitter: outline, symbols, folding, file-level navigation) beside the Red Hat server, never instead of it; parked behind the memory measurement of RFC 0001 decision 1 |

**Settled** — none implemented, rejected or superseded: history rather than proposals.
